data.title: Wheat Futures Recover on Russia-Ukraine Strife — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

  • Wheat for December delivery rose 1.5% on the Chicago Board of Trade Friday to $5.93 1/4 a bushel as Russia and Ukraine continue strikes after this week's talks failed to produce an agreement to ease Black Sea tensions.
  • Soybeans for January delivery rose 1% to $12.31 1/2 a bushel.
  • Corn for December delivery rose 0.7% to $4.45 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

Bouncing Back: Wheat futures rebound back from the previous day's losses as Russia and Ukraine step up strikes, with no deal seen to ease Black Sea shipping. Brazil cut its 2026 wheat production estimate to 5.3 million metric tons from 5.7 million tons, while Argentina's Rosario exchange raised its wheat forecast for the country to 24.3 million tons from 23.8 million tons.

Mixed Export Sales: The USDA reported corn export sales of 3.48 million metric tons for last week, including a marketing-year high 2.88 million tons for 2026/27 and 594,400 tons for 2027/28. Soybean sales fell 21% from the week before to 1.15 million tons for 2026/27, with an additional 11,200 tons sold for 2027/28. Wheat export sales fell 66% from the previous week to 182,800 tons, a marketing-year low.

Flash Sales: Private exporters reported sales of 303,300 metric tons of corn to Mexico--272,820 tons for the 2026/27 marketing year and 30,480 tons for 2027/28, the USDA said. In addition, soybean sales for 2026/27 included 134,000 tons to China, 120,000 tons to Vietnam and 100,000 tons to unknown destinations

INSIGHT

More Please: Last week's U.S. corn export sales, equivalent to 113.4 million bushels for 2026/27, were the largest for any week since January and the most on record for the comparable week, said Mike Castle of StoneX. "These are the kind of weeks corn bulls need to see help the weak 2026/27 cumulative sales pace play catch-up." Export sales are still lagging last year by 27.8%, Castle added in a note.

Steady Outlook: Brazilian national supply company Conab held its estimate for the 2026/27 soybean harvest at 181.6 million metric tons, with planting 66.8% complete as of the first week of November. Initial development has been generally positive, but conditions have varied across regions, the state company said. "Irregular rainfall, combined with high temperatures and the effects of the El Niño phenomenon at the start of this cycle, calls for a cautious outlook regarding productive potential." Conab sees corn production from its three harvests reaching 148 million tons, also unchanged from October, with higher planted area compared with last year partially offset by lower yields.

AHEAD

  • Tyson Foods Inc. will release its 4Q 2026 earnings report before the market opens Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.
  • The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.
  • The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10"30 a.m. Wednesday

Write to Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com

data.title: ICE Review: Canola Continues to Climb
data.description:

At mid-afternoon, the Canadian dollar was down more than one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared to Thursday's close.

data.title: Two-year yields headed for biggest weekly jump in two years
data.description:
Key points:
  • Two-year yields headed for largest weekly gain in two years
  • Traders expect faster pace of rate hikes due to elevated inflation
  • October producer price gains below economists' expectations

By Karen Brettell

Interest rate-sensitive 2-year Treasury yields are headed for the largest weekly increase in more than two years on Friday, after hotter-than-expected consumer price inflation and hawkish Federal Reserve commentary this week led traders to ramp up bets on faster interest rate increases.

Treasury yields briefly dipped on Friday after data showed that producer price inflation was lower than economists expected in October, though it showed the largest annual gain in four years.

Yields remain sharply higher on the week as traders see rising odds that the US central bank could hike rates by a larger-than-usual 50 basis points in December, or raise rates by 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings.

“Inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed's going to need to act a little bit quicker and a little bit more aggressively,” said Molly Brooks, US rates strategist at TD Securities.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December 8-9 meeting, compared with zero probability a week ago, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch Tool.

The odds of the Fed hiking rates by a cumulative 50 basis points by January have risen to 67%, from 16% a week ago, while 75 basis points of hikes by March has a 48% chance, up from 6% a week ago.

The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield was last up 0.34 basis point at 4.867%. It earlier reached 4.892%, the highest since October 14, and is headed for the biggest weekly increase since the first week of October 2024.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 4.64 basis points to 5.149%. It reached 5.174%, the highest since October 14, and is on track for its biggest weekly rise since the April 2025 "tariff tantrum."

The closely watched yield curve between 2- and 10-year notes (US2US10=TWEB) steepened to 28 basis points. It reached 21 basis points on Thursday, the flattest level since September 24.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the prospect of a larger-than-usual 50-basis-point hike in December when he said on Tuesday that the central bank should consider a half-point increase if the inflation picture worsens.

A heavy slate of Fed speakers since then has also bolstered the case that a faster pace of rate hikes may be needed to stem inflation, which has been running above the Fed’s 2% annual target for almost six years.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Friday that tighter monetary policy is coming because of high inflation, in comments that suggested the US central bank may have to raise interest rates more than she initially expected.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that her "bias" is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, particularly with services inflation moving in the wrong direction and some signs of inflation persistence.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said that price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices, contradicting comments by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that the Fed should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war.

Concerns about the ongoing war with Iran have added to the move higher in rates. US President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US did not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete and total attention" on what Trump said were crime and corruption in Democratic-led cities and states.

data.title: Deep Isolation Reports Q3 2026 Revenue of $1.8 Million and Net Loss of $3.8 Million
data.description:
Deep Isolation reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $1.787 million and a net loss of $3.764 million. Gross profit was $957,000, while operating loss was $3.855 million. The company ended the quarter with $16.540 million in cash and continued work on its full-scale, non-radioactive deep borehole demonstration in Texas.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $1.787 million, compared with $1.683 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was $957,000, compared with $983,000 a year earlier.
  • Operating loss was $3.855 million, compared with $1.539 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net loss was $3.764 million, or $0.07 per basic and diluted share, compared with a net loss of $1.307 million, or $0.02 per share, a year earlier.
  • Adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.369 million; cash was $16.540 million as of September 30, 2026.

Business Highlights

  • The company’s common stock began trading on the OTCQB Venture Market in July.
  • Deep Isolation was selected as the sole industrial partner on three Department of Energy Project GENESIS grants focused on AI-enabled repository site screening, design and performance analysis.
  • A three-year DOE-funded study assessed disposal of waste from recycled nuclear fuel. The company reported that all scenarios studied were projected below the program’s cost target and met safety performance criteria under expected conditions.
  • For its non-radioactive Commercialization Pilot near Cameron, Texas, the company received a drilling permit from the Texas Railroad Commission after quarter-end and began site preparation, including well pad construction.
  • A customer case study with Slovenia’s Agency for Radioactive Waste Management examined integration of research-reactor spent fuel into a proposed deep borehole repository for Krško Nuclear Power Plant spent fuel.

data.title: FAA revises SpaceX Starship license, authorizes single Flight 15 launch
data.description:
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has issued a revised commercial space transportation license authorizing SpaceX to conduct a single Starship-Super Heavy Flight 15 launch, along with associated Starship reentry operations.

The license, numbered VOL 23-129 Rev. 10.0, was issued on November 13, 2026, by the FAA's Office of Commercial Space Transportation. It authorizes pre-flight ground operations at SpaceX's Boca Chica Launch Complex in Starbase, Texas, and flights from the facility.

Under the revised authorization, the Super Heavy booster may land in the Gulf of America or return to the launch complex, while Starship's authorized suborbital destination is an Indian Ocean location, as specified in the application.

A separate order, A-2, authorizes Starship reentry from Earth orbit to the Pacific Ocean, the Gulf of America, or the Boca Chica launch complex, subject to the mission profiles represented in SpaceX's application. The reentry authorization also applies to a single operation following Flight 15.

The accompanying financial responsibility orders require SpaceX to maintain $500 million in liability insurance for launch operations and $500 million for covered claims associated with reentry at each of the three authorized destinations. Government property insurance requirements are set at zero dollars for the specified launch and reentry activities.

The revised license retains environmental compliance, mitigation, monitoring, and reporting obligations, including annual certification of compliance with applicable environmental requirements. SpaceX must also report specified operational anomalies and environmental violations to the FAA.

The license retains its original five-year term, terminating on April 14, 2028.

data.title: YES Bank files review petition in SC over Rs.8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-down
data.description:
Mumbai, Nov. 13 -- YES Bank has asked the Supreme Court to review its 15 October order upholding a Bombay High Court ruling against the write-down of Rs.8,415 crore of additional tier-1 (AT-1) bonds, a move that could prolong the wait for bondholders.

"The Bank has filed a review petition under Article 137 of the Constitution of India before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India seeking review of its judgment and order dated October 15, 2026 in relation to the write-down of additional tier-1 bonds aggregating to Rs.8,415 crore," the lender said in a late Friday disclosure to the stock exchanges.

In its 15 October ruling, the Supreme Court dismissed appeals by YES Bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Centre, upholding a Bombay High Court order that held that the bank's administrator had no authority to write down the bonds as part of the lender's 2020 rescue.

The case relates to the perpetual AT-1 bonds that were written down as part of the YES Bank Reconstruction Scheme, 2020. Bondholders and the trustee, Axis Trustee Services, challenged the decision before the Bombay High Court, which quashed the write-down in January 2023.

The Supreme court directed YES Bank to restore the bonds to bondholders with immediate effect. However, with the lender yet to act on the judgment, the YES Bank AT-1 Bond Holders Association, which represents around 400-450 affected investors, and Axis Trustee Services have written to the bank seeking restoration of the bonds and payment of pending interest dues.

"The bank will take all such steps and measures as are necessary and permissible under applicable law," including consequential actions, available legal remedies and other steps that may appropriately be taken in accordance with the law, it said in a letter to Axis Trustee dated 30 October.

The lender has reiterated the same in other public disclosures, and has also informed stakeholders that it is continuing to evaluate and assess the matter

Shares of YES Bank ended 0.3% lower at Rs.17.42 on the National Stock Exchange on Friday.

Reinstating the bonds is expected to have a significant capital and margin impact for the lender. In the earnings call, managing director and chief executive director Vinay Tonse had said that reinstatement of the AT-1 principal amount is expected to have a pro forma impact of approximately 240 basis points on the bank's common equity tier-1 ratio, including profits. As of 30 September, the bank's capital adequacy ratio was 14.5% and the common equity tier-1 ratio was 13.7%.

"Our overall Tier 1 capital ratio is expected to remain around 13.7% on a pro forma basis. We recognize that the distinction between CET-1 and overall Tier 1 capital is important. We will continue to assess the implications for our capital structure, regulatory buffers, balance Sheet strength, and future growth plans," Tonse had said.

data.title: Commodity-Trading Chief Calls for Aluminum Pricing Reform, U.S. Futures — WSJ
data.description:
By Ryan Dezember

The top U.S. commodity-futures market regulator said Friday that he has asked his staff to develop "reform options" for domestic aluminum markets, including U.S. futures contracts.

Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig made his comments to a beer-industry gathering in Washington, D.C. as President Trump's 50% aluminum tariff has pushed the domestic benchmark to a record premium over global prices. The Midwest Premium, calculated by S&P Global Energy's Platts, has lately added more than 75% to the price set by traders in London's metals trading pits.

"The concern is that American manufacturers, including our beer producers here, can face prices incorporating costs that don't actually reflect supply chains through a benchmark structure poorly aligned with U.S. physical metals markets," Selig said.

The daily Midwest Premium price assessment is based on actual sales and reflects the cost of supplying aluminum to the U.S., a Platts spokeman said, adding that the methodology is publicly available and has been rigorously tested.

The CFTC doesn't set commodity prices, but it is exploring the potential for U.S.-based futures contracts tied to physical delivery for both primary and recycled aluminum, Selig said.

Though primary aluminum production has dwindled in the U.S. because of relatively high energy costs, aluminum recycling facilities, which require far less electricity than smelters, have proliferated.

"One of my goals is to strengthen this derivatives market by working closely with various stakeholders to develop a derivatives market structure specifically for recycled aluminum," Selig said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: AI-NATIVE SOFTWARE COMPANIES LEAD ON GROWTH, BUT STRONGER ECONOMICS HAVE NOT YET FOLLOWED
data.description:
17th annual benchmark from KeyBanc Capital Markets, formerly the SaaS Survey, expands to measure how AI is reshaping the private software industry

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KeyBanc Capital Markets Inc., the corporate and investment banking unit of KeyCorp (), today released results from its 17th annual AI x Software Benchmark, one of the longest-running benchmarks of financial and operating performance by software companies. Formerly known as the SaaS Survey, the benchmark has been expanded this year to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing product strategy, monetization, unit economics, and operating models.

This year's findings show that companies selling AI as their primary product are growing significantly faster than their peers, but they also report weaker profitability and revenue productivity than software companies embedding AI into existing products. AI adoption is widespread; monetization and measurable financial impact remain early.

"For 17 years, this benchmark has given software operators and investors a clear view of how the industry is performing. This year, the central question is whether AI is creating a durable advantage," said Scott Peterson, Managing Director, Software Investment Banking at KeyBanc Capital Markets. " AI is accelerating growth and compressing development cycles, but AI spend is running ahead of budget and the economics are still catching up. 2026 is a proving year for AI-driven revenue."

"Developer headcount has historically been one of the biggest constraints for software development. AI coding tools are loosening that constraint as developer productivity improves," added Peterson. "But rather than let those gains drop to the bottom line, companies are reinvesting them to ship more product faster."

TOP TRENDS AND INSIGHTS:

AI-native companies lead on growth, while embedded AI leads on economics

  • Companies selling AI as their primary product reported median ARR growth of 34% in 2025, compared with 22% for companies embedding AI in broader products and 9% for companies still developing customer-facing AI.
  • Core AI product companies reported a median EBITDA margin of (12%) in 2025, compared with (1%) for embedded AI companies
  • Embedded AI companies also led on productivity, with ARR per FTE at $201K versus $117K for core AI product companies.
  • Companies that charge separately for AI products reported 27% median ARR growth in 2025, versus 17% for those that do not. That growth advantage has not yet translated into higher net retention.

AI revenue is small but poised to accelerate quickly

  • AI-driven ARR is projected to grow 128% in 2026, up from 74% in 2025, yet will still only represent 12% of total ARR.
  • Overall median ARR growth was 24% in 2025 and is projected at 23% in 2026, with participants planning for a broad-based acceleration to 40% in 2027.
  • Overall median EBITDA margin is expected to improve from (3%) in 2025 to 1% in 2026.

AI spend is outpacing budgets and showing up in margins before growth

  • More than four in 10 respondents (44%) report AI spend over budget year to date, and roughly a quarter (24%) are over by more than 20%. Higher-than-expected token usage was the most cited driver of variance.
  • Companies spending more than 5% of revenue on AI reported a median gross margin of 66% in 2025, compared with 78% for those spending less than 2%.

AI is speeding up product development, and workforce impact expected to broaden

  • 92% of respondents report that AI is shortening product development cycles, and 91% deploy AI internally in engineering.
  • 65% of participants report no AI-related headcount reduction or reallocation in 2025. Looking out 12 to 24 months, which falls to 34% with R&D (45%) and customer service (37%) the functions most likely to be affected.

Customers are building with AI, while autonomous agents remain early

  • 57% of respondents say their customers are building alternative products with AI coding tools.
  • Only 20% offer fully autonomous agents to their customers.

The 2026 AI x Software Benchmark is available for download at key.com.

data.title: Wall St slides as Nvidia uncertainty drags tech shares lower
data.description:
Key points:
  • Microsoft edges up after global outage eases
  • Nvidia falls further following Jensen Huang's exit
  • Indexes down: Dow 0.01%, S&P 500 0.51%, Nasdaq 0.93%

By Chuck Mikolajczak and Niket Nishant

US stocks were lower on Friday, as concerns about Nvidia pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

Nvidia's shares fell 2.2% and were poised for their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, following revelations of his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The uncertainty about leadership at the chipmaker has raised concerns about the durability of the AI trade, given Nvidia's primary role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to several companies in the sector, which has been a pillar of the bull market in equities.

"The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia is going to go through a period of volatility, and you're going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there's been a loss of confidence," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan.

"The market and investors are trying to navigate what does the AI theme look like when we have the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia's balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That's gone."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 5.36 points, or 0.01%, to 52,291.73, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 38.87 points, or 0.51%, to 7,553.53 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 236.49 points, or 0.93%, to 25,129.60.

Despite the recent volatility, the major indexes were on track for weekly gains, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 both set to snap a four-week streak of declines.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.7%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom the biggest drags.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also slumped, while data center-related firms IREN and Applied Digital retreated as well.

The losses come ahead of AI company Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO next week, which could test investor appetite for established AI heavyweights as money potentially shifts toward the new entrant.

The S&P 500 technology index was off 1.6% as the worst-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. But Microsoft shares edged up 0.4% after a global outage that included its Outlook and Teams products began to ease.

INFLATION CONCERNS REMAIN

On the economic front, the Labor Department said US producer prices were slightly cooler than expected in October, but still shot up 6.5% year over year, the largest annual gain since November 2022.

The data kept expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed's December meeting completely locked in, with markets pricing in a roughly 10% chance for an outsized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

The sentiment for additional rate hikes was echoed by more Fed officials on Friday, including San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly, who said her "bias" is that the central bank will need to increase its policy rate, while Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said tighter monetary policy is coming because of high inflation.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.42-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and by a 1.78-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 9 new 52-week highs and 1 new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 28 new highs and 301 new lows.
